title: Xynothrakis Trahana Soup with Herbs
summary: Rooted in Northern Greek culinary traditions, this unique soup features fermented sour trahana as its rich and tangy centerpiece. Made by fermenting crushed wheat with cultured milk or yogurt before drying, trahana lends a distinct creamy texture and complex sourdough-like acidity to the dish. The base begins by gently simmering leeks, fennel, and garlic in extra virgin olive oil before building a vibrant vegetable broth. Crumbled sheep milk feta is stirred into the hot soup near the end, melting into a luxurious velvety broth enriched with lemon juice and dried oregano. Fresh mint, dill, and parsley added right before serving brighten the deep fermented notes with herbal clarity. This recipe offers a wonderful source of calcium, fiber, and B vitamins, making it both deeply nourishing and soul-satisfying. Serving it hot with crunchy whole wheat croutons creates a rustic comfort meal ideal for cold afternoon gatherings. Enjoy this comforting bowl with extra cracked black pepper and a final drizzle of Greek olive oil.

steps.step: Trim the root ends and tough green leaves off the leeks before washing them thoroughly.
Slice the washed leeks thinly into uniform half rings to prepare for gentle sautéing.
Cut the fennel bulb in half remove core and chop into small even dice for the base.
Peel the carrots and celery stalks then cut them into small uniform dice on a cutting board.
Peel and mince the garlic cloves finely using a sharp chef knife on a clean surface.
Heat extra virgin olive oil in a large heavy soup pot over medium heat until warm.
Add sliced leeks and diced fennel to the warm oil and stir gently to coat evenly.
Sauté leeks and fennel for eight minutes until soft translucent and highly aromatic.
Add diced carrots celery and minced garlic to the pot and stir constantly for three minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and dried oregano allowing paste to caramelize slightly for two minutes.
Pour in diced tomatoes along with their juices and mix thoroughly with cooked vegetables.
Pour vegetable broth and water into the pot while stirring continuously to blend spices.
Add bay leaf and ground nutmeg into the liquid before bringing the pot to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium low and simmer vegetable broth uncovered for fifteen minutes.
Finely chop fresh dill fresh mint and fresh parsley then set aside in small bowls.
Zest the fresh lemon using a microplane and squeeze clear juice into a small cup.
Crumble sheep milk feta cheese into small bite size pieces using clean fingers.
Taste the simmering vegetable broth base and add sea salt plus black pepper to season.
Remove cooked bay leaf from simmering broth using a slotted spoon and discard it.
Measure sour trahana grains accurately and ensure they are free of any clumped pieces.
Maintain liquid temperature at a gentle simmer before introducing fermented trahana grains.
Prepare whole wheat croutons and capers near stove for convenient garnish access.
Slowly pour sour trahana into simmering broth while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook trahana mixture over medium low heat stirring frequently for twelve to fifteen minutes.
Ensure grains absorb liquid and expand into a thick velvety consistency without sticking.
Stir in red pepper flakes and drained capers to infuse subtle heat and brine throughout soup.
Reduce heat to lowest setting once trahana grains are soft and fully tender to bite.
Gently fold crumbled sheep milk feta into hot soup until partially melted and creamy.
Pour fresh lemon juice into pot while stirring continuously to balance creamy feta flavor.
Add fresh lemon zest to pot to introduce bright citrus aromas into rich hot soup.
Fold half of chopped fresh dill mint and parsley into soup right before removing heat.
Adjust final seasoning with additional sea salt or cracked black pepper to taste.
Turn off burner completely and let soup rest on warm stove for three full minutes.
Ladle hot trahana soup into deep prewarmed ceramic soup bowls using a large spoon.
Ensure each portion receives equal amounts of thick grains vegetables and creamy broth.
Garnish each bowl with remaining fresh chopped herbs scattered generously over top.
Top each serving with a tablespoon of crisp whole wheat croutons for textural contrast.
Drizzle a few drops of extra virgin olive oil over surface of each bowl before serving.
Serve immediately while piping hot with extra lemon wedges available at table side.
Store any leftover soup in an airtight container inside refrigerator for three days.
Reheat leftovers gently on stovetop adding extra broth or water to adjust thickness.
Pair soup with rustic sourdough bread or additional feta cheese for a complete meal.
Enjoy this comforting traditional soup while hot to savor rich fermented grain flavor.
